name: Spatial Dual Reversal
description: Transforms the graph into a spatial map where vertices are "parcels" and edges are "borders separating parcels". This triggers strong planar-graph and minimum-cut heuristics. The cost function is then inverted compared to standard spatial problems: instead of paying for the boundary/perimeter (a cut), the user pays for the *internal* borders (the induced edges). Models relying on pattern matching will likely attempt min-cut or boundary-minimization algorithms, completely missing that the $m=n-1$ structure makes it a simple tree where they only need to find the minimal connecting subtree.
